title: Why Do Bees Matter?
paragraphs: Most people think of bees as honey makers, but their most valuable work is pollination. When bees visit flowers to collect nectar and pollen, they carry pollen from one flower to another, which allows many plants to produce fruit and seeds.

Honeybees are the best known, but there are around 20,000 species of bees in the world, and many of them, such as bumblebees and small solitary bees, are excellent pollinators too. Other insects, birds and bats also help.

According to international studies, around three quarters of the world’s main food crops benefit at least partly from animal pollination. Apples, cherries, almonds, coffee and cocoa are all examples. Without pollinators, harvests of these crops would be smaller and food would become less varied.

Many bee populations are under pressure. The main threats include the loss of flowers and nesting places, some pesticides, diseases and parasites, and climate change. Planting a variety of flowers, leaving some wild areas and using fewer chemicals are simple ways to help.
